problems.title: Mass of an ideal gas
problems.scenario:
A rigid tank of volume **2.0 m³** holds air at **500 kPa** and **300 K**. Take $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the **mass** of air in the tank.
hints: Use the ideal-gas law $PV = mRT$ and solve for $m$.
$m = PV/(RT)$. Keep pressure in kPa and $R$ in kJ/(kg·K) so units cancel to kg.
Temperature must be absolute (300 K — already is).
problems.solution:
Rearrange the ideal-gas equation $PV = mRT$ for mass:

$$m = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{(500)(2.0)}{(0.287)(300)} = \frac{1000}{86.1} = 11.61\ \text{kg}$$

Units: $\text{kPa}\cdot\text{m}^3 / (\text{kJ/(kg·K)}\cdot\text{K}) = \text{kJ}/(\text{kJ/kg}) = \text{kg}$. ✓

problems.title: Gas constant of CO₂
problems.scenario:
Carbon dioxide has a molar mass $M = 44.0\ \text{kg/kmol}$. The universal gas constant is $R_u = 8.314\ \text{kJ/(kmol·K)}$.

Find the **specific gas constant** $R$ of CO₂.
hints: $R = R_u / M$.
Just divide: $8.314 / 44.0$.
problems.solution:
The specific gas constant is the universal constant per unit molar mass:

$$R = \frac{R_u}{M} = \frac{8.314}{44.0} = 0.189\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

Heavier molecules → smaller $R$. (For comparison, air's is 0.287.)

problems.title: Quality from specific volume
problems.scenario:
A rigid vessel contains water at **200 kPa** with a specific volume of $v = 0.60\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$.

Using $v_f = 0.001061$ and $v_g = 0.88578\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$ at 200 kPa, find the **quality** $x$.
hints: Since $v_f < v < v_g$, the water is a saturated mixture — quality applies.
Start from $v = v_f + x\,v_{fg}$ and rearrange for $x$.
problems.solution:
The specific volume lies between $v_f$ and $v_g$, so it's a wet mixture. Rearrange the mixture relation for quality:

$$v = v_f + x\,v_{fg} \quad\Rightarrow\quad x = \frac{v - v_f}{v_g - v_f}$$

$$x = \frac{0.60 - 0.001061}{0.88578 - 0.001061} = \frac{0.598939}{0.884719} = 0.677$$

So about 68% of the mass is vapour.

problems.title: Enthalpy of a saturated mixture
problems.scenario:
Water at **200 kPa** has a quality of **x = 0.70**.

Using $h_f = 504.7\ \text{kJ/kg}$ and $h_{fg} = 2201.6\ \text{kJ/kg}$ at 200 kPa, find the **specific enthalpy** $h$.
hints: Use the mixture property relation with enthalpy.
Just substitute the table values.
problems.solution:
Any property of a saturated mixture is the quality-weighted value:

$$h = h_f + x\,h_{fg} = 504.7 + 0.70 \times 2201.6$$

$$h = 504.7 + 1541.1 = 2045.8\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

The same $y = y_f + x\,y_{fg}$ form works for $v$, $u$, and $s$ too.

problems.title: Constant-volume heating (combined gas law)
problems.scenario:
An ideal gas in a **rigid** container is at **100 kPa** and **300 K**. It is heated to **400 K**.

Find the **final pressure**.
hints: Rigid → volume constant, so $V_1 = V_2$ drops out of the combined gas law.
Temperatures must be absolute (they're in K already).
problems.solution:
For a fixed mass of ideal gas, $\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$. With constant volume ($V_1 = V_2$) this reduces to Gay-Lussac's law:

$$\frac{P_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2}{T_2} \quad\Rightarrow\quad P_2 = P_1\,\frac{T_2}{T_1}$$

$$P_2 = 100 \times \frac{400}{300} = 133.3\ \text{kPa}$$

Pressure rises in proportion to absolute temperature when volume is fixed.

problems.title: Vapour mass in a rigid tank
problems.scenario:
A rigid tank of **0.50 m³** holds water at **300 kPa** with quality **x = 0.60**.

Using $v_f = 0.001073$ and $v_g = 0.60582\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$ at 300 kPa, find the **mass of vapour** in the tank.
hints: Three steps: find $v$ from quality, then total mass $m = V/v$, then vapour mass $m_g = x\,m$.
$m = V/v$, then $m_g = x\,m$.
problems.solution:
**Step 1 — mixture specific volume:**

$$v = v_f + x\,(v_g - v_f) = 0.001073 + 0.60(0.60582 - 0.001073) = 0.001073 + 0.36285 = 0.36392\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$$

**Step 2 — total mass** from $v = V/m$:

$$m = \frac{V}{v} = \frac{0.50}{0.36392} = 1.374\ \text{kg}$$

**Step 3 — vapour mass** is the quality fraction of the total:

$$m_g = x\,m = 0.60 \times 1.374 = 0.824\ \text{kg}$$

problems.title: Real-gas specific volume (compressibility)
problems.scenario:
Nitrogen ($R = 0.2968\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$) is at **8 MPa** and **150 K**. From the generalized compressibility chart, **Z = 0.84** at this state.

Find the **actual specific volume**, in m³/kg.
hints: First get the ideal-gas estimate $v_{ideal} = RT/P$ (use 8 MPa = 8000 kPa).
Then correct it with $Z$: $v = Z\,v_{ideal}$.
Equivalently, $v = ZRT/P$.
problems.solution:
Near its critical region nitrogen deviates from ideal-gas behaviour, so we scale the ideal estimate by $Z$:

$$v_{ideal} = \frac{RT}{P} = \frac{0.2968 \times 150}{8000} = \frac{44.52}{8000} = 0.005565\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$$

$$v = Z\,v_{ideal} = 0.84 \times 0.005565 = 0.004675\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}$$

With $Z = 0.84 < 1$ the real gas is more compressed than the ideal model predicts — ignoring $Z$ would overestimate the volume by ~19%.

problems.title: Mass added to a tank
problems.scenario:
A rigid tank holds **5.0 kg** of air at **200 kPa**, **300 K**. More air is pumped in until the tank reaches **500 kPa**, **350 K**. Take $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the **mass of air added**.
hints: The tank volume is fixed — find it from the initial state: $V = m_1 R T_1/P_1$.
Then find the final mass $m_2 = P_2 V/(R T_2)$.
Mass added $= m_2 - m_1$.
problems.solution:
**Step 1 — tank volume** from the initial state ($PV = mRT$):

$$V = \frac{m_1 R T_1}{P_1} = \frac{5.0 \times 0.287 \times 300}{200} = \frac{430.5}{200} = 2.1525\ \text{m}^3$$

**Step 2 — final mass** at the new state (same $V$):

$$m_2 = \frac{P_2 V}{R T_2} = \frac{500 \times 2.1525}{0.287 \times 350} = \frac{1076.25}{100.45} = 10.71\ \text{kg}$$

**Step 3 — mass added:**

$$\Delta m = m_2 - m_1 = 10.71 - 5.0 = 5.71\ \text{kg}$$
